messages.author: 40eb82e16832af38
messages.subject: Warning messages with blavCompare()
parts:
Hi, I am using blavCompare() to get out the log-bayes factor. The bsem() I am using for comparison was able to converge with no warnings, but the blavCompare() itself is showing these four warning messages:
1: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
 
2: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
 
3: 
23 (8.8%) p_waic estimates greater than 0.4. We recommend trying loo instead. 
4: 
22 (8.5%) p_waic estimates greater than 0.4. We recommend trying loo instead.

I have tried re-running the bsem() models from scratch, and relocating additional memory to R to no avail. Are there any other solution I can try?

Here is formula of my model ( I am using the dplyr library):
ef.formula = '
  wm =~ wm_os + wm_rs + wm_ss
  ic =~ ic_si + ic_fl + ic_st
  ts =~ ts_as + ts_cs + ts_mp
'
h1spa.formula = '
  wm ~ smartphoneAddiction
  ic ~ smartphoneAddiction
  ts ~ smartphoneAddiction
  '%>%paste(ef.formula)
h0spa.nowm.formula = '
  ic ~ smartphoneAddiction
  ts ~ smartphoneAddiction
  '%>%paste(ef.formula)

# bsem model
h1spa.bresult = h1spa.formula %>%
  bsem(data = data.raw, target = "stan", sample = 2000, bcontrol = list(cores = 3))

h0spa.nowm.bresult = h0spa.nowm.formula %>%
  bsem(data = data.raw, target = "stan", sample = 2000, bcontrol = list(cores = 3))

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Warning messages with blavCompare()
parts:
Wei Ming,

This warning message comes from the loo package and is fairly common. The help page that they refer to, which provides some more information, can be accessed via

library(loo)
?pareto-k-diagnostics

The warning applies only to the waic computation, and not to loo or to the log-Bayes factor. But I would be cautious with using the log-Bayes factor reported by blavCompare(), because it is an approximation that is not necessarily precise.

Ed

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Warning messages with blavCompare()
parts:
Wei

The Bayes Factor should be seen as a specific tool for specific cases, it is not stable enough to work as a general model comparison metric. You can see general recommendations on how to work with the BF
https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.08744

A main issue for which I dont recommend it in BSEM, is that it is very sensitive to priors (even with large samples), and not reliable with large dimensional models (which most SEM models are). So, it would require more detail work in evaluating the reliability and accuracy of the BF with some forms of simulation for each specific data sets and models (as explain in the previously mentione paper).

that is why I recommend better the LOO as a general comparison metric, as it compares out-of-sample predictive accuracy, and the metric is less sensitive to priors, model, and data characterictics than BF. Now, nothing is perfect so you it has issue as well, but with largish enough data dets, well defined models, and not super wide priors, works reliably in most cases  https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.10296

MGV
